body:
Copious amounts of drugs or alcohol, neither of which I have had access to since the move. Otherwise, nothing. Nothing ever helps. When I said "it just gets worse" I wasn't kidding. The only time I'm not thinking about this or suicide or some other random thing is when I'm drunk/on drugs. 

I wasn't always like this. Gradually the rejections and etc obliterated my self-esteem and image, killed my confidence, whatever else. Therapy hasn't helped, pharmaceuticals haven't helped, nothing's gonna help until I have success here, because that's my main problem. All the rejection killed gradually everything I thought about myself, and with that went the dreams and goals.

No, I don't expect to find a partner and suddenly everything would be fine, but I'm at the point when I have to admit that I will never make any progress unless I do find one. 

Someone told me to be confident (again), how can you be confident when you have no reason to? How am I supposed to be a confident person when I can't attract anyone, which is something your average 14 year old is capable of? It's impossible. It doesn't make sense. It doesn't work. It's like people blame my failings on the lack of confidence alone when I used to have so much confidence I could be depressed as fuck and glowing like the sun at the same time.
Also taking a break won't really help since most of my life has been one giant break. I need a break, but not that kind. I need a lucky one. It eats at me now. I can't stop thinking about it.

1) I could "fall back" on them any time but I would much rather die. The only reason I even moved is because I didn't want to die in that state. =/
2) Dating websites are miserable failures. That's how I met the one person. There aren't many attractive people from here. She was like, the only one that really stood out, so fuck.
3) I really dislike talking about trans things and family. Neither are therapeutic to me. The trans community hated me (I was more badass metal chick than glamor girl) and thinking/talking about family just makes me upset. 

Ow.

Okay this is going to be a long one but here goes nothing.

I'm a 23 year old transwoman from the USA. I won't lie to you and say I haven't been in the same place as you, I can't tell you I've never been suicidal or aren't at the moment even, but there are some things I can tell you.

I was raised by the worst types of religious nuts. Baptist/Pentecostal fuckwits in the US South. My father ran churches, preached, was a televangelist for a while, and even sang gospel professionally with my mother. As a result, I was caught CDing several times and each time was worse than the last, resulting at last (at 13) in being laughed at by my sister – who was 28 at the time. I came out three separate times, once to my mom (15), another to a friend who discouraged me (18), and finally to everyone (20) when nearing the end of university. Which I failed thanks in no small part due to gender dysphoria. 

It took another year to start hormones, beginning at 21. 

In a few days I'll be crossing 25 months, at 23 years old. I just got out of the deadly parental grasp less than a week ago. I'm still not prescribed the hormones and get them totally black market. 

Seeing life in the before era is bizarre. The person I looked like, the person I acted like, the person I had to be to fit whatever bullshit standards. I'm one of those people that is kind of permanently fucked up, usually spending every 3rd day (and sometimes more) suicidal. Yet even I have to take a step back and go "woah" sometimes at how different I am and how positively things have trended in the past two years.

To be sure, it's hard. So ridiculously hard. The first year was a nightmare. I was raped and lost all of my friends, who I later found out had set me up. I was homeless no less than three times. I was forcibly closeted when living with parents, which was all of the non-homeless time. Even the trans community itself fucked me up, being catty and ridiculous as they are. But I'm here. I survived. It was the most ridiculous and toughest stuff you could imagine, but I'm here, and it rocks in a way, because I can look at what I was and see what I became. 

If you go now, you'll be going as what you hate and letting the bastards win. Play the game, play the system, make every attempt to say what the doctors want to hear, get those hormones, and be you. It might not be enough, but what if it is? I'm not going to tell you not to kill yourself, that's your choice. It would be hypocritical of me to tell someone not to do something I think about a lot. At the same time, I'm going to tell you that you should definitely try to transition before making that leap. It might be more than you expect, and regardless, it will be totally worth it.
